LESSON: AUDIENCE AWARENESS

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SPEAKING
Topic 2.4: Audience Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Audience Awareness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when singing songs, telling stories and to moves away from to others in and out of reciting poems or rhymes. me?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya
3. practise Audience Awareness in clear steps
4. apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: AUDIENCE AWARENESS
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Audience Awareness helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: AUDIENCE AWARENESS
Study Audience Awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Audience Awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Audience Awareness to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Audience Awareness in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Audience Awareness in clear steps. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Audience Awareness in clear steps.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Audience Awareness in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Audience Awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Audience Awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Audience Awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Audience Awareness to a partner. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: practise Audience Awareness in clear steps)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Audience Awareness”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply Audience Awareness in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Audience Awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Audience Awareness in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Audience Awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Audience Awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Audience Awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when singing songs, telling stories and to moves away from to others in and out of reciting poems or rhymes. me?
2. when speaker and the listener is varied. The further away?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Audience Awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Audience Awareness means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Audience Awareness from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
